stories.title: Is AI making your managers stupid ?
stories.summary: McGraw Hill collaborated with researchers from the University of California, Irvine (UC Irvine) to analyze a decade of learning data from its online math platform, revealing insights into how AI integration affects student performance and critical thinking.
stories.why_it_matters: The research provides empirical evidence on the impact of AI in educational settings, highlighting the importance of using AI as a pedagogical tool rather than a shortcut to ensure long-term learning outcomes.
verified_facts: McGraw Hill partnered with UC Irvine researchers to analyze a decade of data from its online math platform.
The study examined 3.2 million learning interactions starting in 2015.
Data showed that after the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, students spent less time on text-based problems but saw a decline in performance on proctored tests.
warnings: The article discusses broader industry trends regarding AI and management, which are not specific to McGraw Hill's corporate operations.
The research findings are based on a preprint study; further peer review may be pending.

drafts.concise: New research conducted by McGraw Hill and the University of California, Irvine, offers a data-driven look at the impact of AI on student learning. By analyzing over 3.2 million interactions on McGraw Hill’s online math platform since 2015, the study highlights a critical shift in student engagement following the introduction of generative AI in 2022. The findings underscore the importance of using AI as a supportive tutor rather than a replacement for independent problem-solving. As the education sector navigates the integration of new technologies, such evidence-based insights are essential for developing effective learning strategies that preserve and enhance critical thinking skills. #EdTech #AI #McGrawHill
drafts.investor: Data-led insights remain a core component of McGraw Hill’s value proposition in the evolving edtech landscape. A recent collaboration with researchers at the University of California, Irvine, utilized a decade of platform data—covering 3.2 million learning interactions—to evaluate the impact of AI on student outcomes. The study provides a nuanced view of how generative AI influences academic performance, reinforcing the necessity for platforms that encourage deep learning over simple automation. This commitment to rigorous research and evidence-based product development ensures that McGraw Hill remains at the forefront of delivering effective, high-quality educational solutions in an increasingly AI-integrated market. #Education #DataScience #Innovation
drafts.people: At McGraw Hill, understanding how students interact with technology is vital to fostering long-term academic success. We are pleased to highlight a significant research collaboration between our team and the University of California, Irvine. By examining 3.2 million learning interactions from our online math platform, the study provides valuable evidence on how AI tools can be best utilized to support, rather than replace, the development of critical thinking. These insights are instrumental in shaping how we design learning experiences that empower students to master complex concepts. Thank you to the researchers and our internal teams for their dedication to evidence-based education. #Learning #Research #EdTech

stories.title: McGraw Hill's Emerge! K-5 Science of Reading Program Included on Pennsylvania's Curriculum Materials List for Evidence-Based Reading Instruction - The Joplin Globe
stories.summary: McGraw Hill's 'Emerge!' K-5 Science of Reading program has been officially included on Pennsylvania's state-approved list of curriculum materials for evidence-based reading instruction.
stories.why_it_matters: State-level curriculum approvals are critical milestones for education publishers, as they validate the efficacy of learning materials and significantly increase the addressable market within public school districts.
verified_facts: McGraw Hill's Emerge! K-5 Science of Reading program is the product in question.
The program has been included on Pennsylvania's curriculum materials list for evidence-based reading instruction.

drafts.concise: We are pleased to share that McGraw Hill’s 'Emerge!' K-5 Science of Reading program has been officially included on Pennsylvania’s list of approved curriculum materials for evidence-based reading instruction. This recognition underscores the program's alignment with rigorous educational standards and its commitment to supporting foundational literacy development in classrooms. By meeting these state-level requirements, McGraw Hill continues to provide educators and students with high-quality, evidence-backed resources designed to improve reading outcomes. Congratulations to the team on this significant achievement in the K-5 space. #Education #Literacy #McGrawHill
drafts.investor: McGraw Hill continues to strengthen its market position in the K-5 sector, with its 'Emerge!' Science of Reading program recently securing a place on Pennsylvania’s list of approved curriculum materials. State-level approvals of this nature are key drivers for adoption, validating the efficacy of the company's learning technology and expanding its footprint within public school districts. This development reflects the ongoing demand for evidence-based pedagogical tools and highlights McGraw Hill's ability to navigate complex regulatory environments to deliver scalable, high-impact educational solutions. #EdTech #Growth #Education
drafts.people: A significant milestone for the McGraw Hill team as their 'Emerge!' K-5 Science of Reading program is now included on Pennsylvania’s list of approved curriculum materials. This achievement is a testament to the hard work and dedication of the product and pedagogical teams who have developed a curriculum grounded in evidence-based reading instruction. It is rewarding to see their commitment to improving literacy outcomes recognised at the state level, ensuring that teachers and students have access to the best possible tools for success. Well done to everyone involved in this accomplishment. #TeamSuccess #Education #ScienceOfReading

sector_stories.title: CWU: Royal Mail stands “on the brink of collapse”
sector_stories.summary: The Communication Workers Union has called for an emergency government summit to address Royal Mail's structural decline and severe recruitment and retention crises.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights significant instability in the UK's primary postal incumbent, potentially impacting market capacity and competitor service expectations.

sector_stories.title: Nearly six in 10 transport firms are ‘very concerned’ about fuel prices, more than any other sector
sector_stories.summary: ONS data shows that 59.8% of transport and storage businesses are now 'very concerned' about rising fuel prices, up from 43% in August.
sector_stories.angle: Rising fuel costs increase operational pressure and necessitate potential adjustments to delivery pricing and surcharges across the sector.

sector_stories.title: Royal Mail Responds to “Misleading Statements” by CWU Leadership
sector_stories.summary: Royal Mail reports improved service quality and is hiring 22,000 seasonal workers while addressing ongoing industrial relations tensions with the Communication Workers Union ahead of the peak season.
sector_stories.angle: Provides critical insight into competitor operational capacity, service performance trends, and potential labour market shifts in UK delivery.

sector_stories.title: Ofcom: Royal Mail’s financial position is stark
sector_stories.summary: Ofcom has proposed extending the current Second Class stamp price cap for one year until March 2028 to allow Royal Mail more time to implement universal service reforms.
sector_stories.angle: Regulatory constraints on the dominant market player influence pricing strategies and service standards across the UK postal sector.

sector_stories.title: Crowd safety can no longer be an afterthought
sector_stories.summary: The Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025, or Martyn’s Law, mandates that public venues and event organisers implement formal security and evacuation procedures to mitigate terrorism risks.
sector_stories.angle: New statutory duties for public venues increase demand for professional security planning, training, and integrated site safety solutions.

sector_stories.title: VPS unveils research paper on pricing metal theft
sector_stories.summary: VPS has published a white paper highlighting that the business disruption costs of metal theft significantly outweigh the scrap value of the stolen materials.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights shifting criminal tactics and the need for risk-based security strategies for critical infrastructure and vacant sites.

sector_stories.title: Slamming the brakes on EV charging crime
sector_stories.summary: Rising theft of copper cables and vandalism at remote EV charging sites is driving demand for proactive, AI-powered video surveillance and remote monitoring solutions.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights a growing, high-value niche for remote site security services in the expanding EV infrastructure market.

sector_stories.title: From duty of care policy to operational readiness
sector_stories.summary: The article discusses the implications of the Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025, known as Martyn’s Law, regarding preparedness and safety procedures at qualifying UK premises.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights regulatory shifts in UK site security and the increasing operational requirements for premises protection and emergency preparedness.

sector_stories.title: Greater range at the same weight: silicon battery passes laboratory test
sector_stories.summary: Researchers at Fraunhofer ISE have successfully tested silicon-rich anode pouch cells, achieving 1,000 cycles with 83 per cent capacity retention and a potential energy density of 330 Wh/kg.
sector_stories.angle: Higher energy density batteries could significantly increase e-bike range or reduce weight, enhancing product performance and portability.

sector_stories.title: London considers mandating BEVs for new ride-hailing licences
sector_stories.summary: Transport for London is consulting on a proposal to mandate that all newly licensed private hire vehicles must be fully battery-electric by 2028.
sector_stories.angle: Signals accelerating urban policy shifts towards zero-emission transport, reinforcing the broader market transition away from combustion-engine vehicles.

sector_stories.title: Belgian Post fleet now features 4,165 electric delivery vans
sector_stories.summary: Belgian postal operator Bpost has expanded its electric fleet to 4,165 vans, while also operating 3,013 electric bicycles and 556 electric bicycle trailers for last-mile delivery.
sector_stories.angle: Demonstrates large-scale institutional adoption of e-bikes and trailers for urban logistics and last-mile delivery efficiency.

sector_stories.title: Green Science Alliance opens Swiss battery recycling lab
sector_stories.summary: Green Science Alliance has opened a battery recycling laboratory in Switzerland to develop direct recycling methods for cathode materials from lithium-ion batteries.
sector_stories.angle: Advancements in direct battery recycling could improve supply chain sustainability and reduce costs for micromobility battery manufacturers.

sector_stories.title: Nvidia’s Editor’s Day: New Windows-Based RTX Spark Computers
sector_stories.summary: Nvidia has launched the RTX Spark line of ARM-based Windows computers, featuring unified memory architectures designed to facilitate local AI processing for creative workflows.
sector_stories.angle: Local AI processing improves security and reliability for post-production workflows, reducing reliance on cloud-based AI tools.

sector_stories.title: Sync.Labs Intros Zero-Shot Lipsyncing for Film and Television
sector_stories.summary: Sync.Labs has launched Sync.Productions, a managed service using AI to perform zero-shot lipsyncing for film and television localization without requiring actor-specific training or facial scans.
sector_stories.angle: AI-driven automated lipsyncing tools are increasingly capable of professional-grade localization, impacting traditional post-production workflows and dubbing services.

sector_stories.title: How Colorist Siggy Ferstl Gave Airbender More Depth in the Grade
sector_stories.summary: Colorist Siggy Ferstl is using AI-driven depth mapping tools in Blackmagic Resolve to perform complex VFX-style adjustments during the final color grading process.
sector_stories.angle: Demonstrates the increasing convergence of traditional color grading and VFX workflows through advanced, real-time software automation.

sector_stories.title: The Look and Color of One Hundred Years of Solitude Part 2
sector_stories.summary: The production team for One Hundred Years of Solitude Part 2 integrated post-production and color workflows into pre-production to ensure visual consistency across a complex, long-term shoot.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights the industry shift toward integrating post-production expertise into early pre-production and on-set workflows for high-end episodic content.

sector_stories.title: Recycled Plastics Market to Reach $117 . 9 Billion by 2031 at 9 % CAGR
sector_stories.summary: The global recycled plastics market is projected to reach $117.9 billion by 2031, driven by regulatory mandates like the EU's PPWR and rising corporate sustainability commitments.
sector_stories.angle: Regulatory recycled-content targets and supply-demand imbalances directly impact PET packaging procurement, pricing, and long-term manufacturing strategy.

sector_stories.title: Regulators intervene over PRN undersupply as FPA calls for fundamental review of 2027 targets
sector_stories.summary: UK regulators have issued a Regulatory Position Statement allowing businesses to meet reduced plastic recycling obligations for 2026 due to a shortage of Packaging Waste Recycling Notes.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights systemic instability in the PRN market and critical upcoming regulatory shifts regarding PET and DRS implementation.

sector_stories.title: EU rules will require cafés & restaurants to accept customers’ reusable containers
sector_stories.summary: New EU regulations mandate that food and drink outlets must allow customers to use their own reusable containers for takeaway services starting 12 February 2027.
sector_stories.angle: Regulatory shift towards reuse and refill models impacts demand for traditional single-use PET packaging in the hospitality sector.

sector_stories.title: Suntory targets 90% value-chain emissions cut with packaging focus
sector_stories.summary: Suntory has announced a climate transition plan targeting a 90% reduction in value-chain emissions by 2050, with a specific focus on sustainable packaging and recycled PET content.
sector_stories.angle: Major beverage brands are increasingly mandating high recycled content and reduced material usage from their packaging suppliers.

sector_stories.title: SUSE unveils sovereign AI platform with NVIDIA tie - up
sector_stories.summary: SUSE has launched a sovereign AI platform integrating NVIDIA hardware and OpenShell architecture to enable secure, private deployment of autonomous AI agents within enterprise environments.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights the industry shift towards integrated, hardware-backed sovereign AI stacks for enterprise data control and governance.

sector_stories.title: UK AI Taskforce Seeks Business - Rate Incentives for Data Center Hosts
sector_stories.summary: The Sovereign AI Leadership taskforce is lobbying the UK government to allow local councils to retain more business rates from data center developments to mitigate public opposition.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights critical infrastructure policy shifts and public sentiment risks impacting the deployment of sovereign AI data centers.

sector_stories.title: World Wide Technology Partners With Polarise to Accelerate Europe Sovereign AI Buildout , Starting in Oslo
sector_stories.summary: Polarise and World Wide Technology have partnered to accelerate the deployment of sovereign AI infrastructure across Europe, beginning with a 5 MW AI data centre in Oslo.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights increasing competition and the role of systems integrators in scaling sovereign AI infrastructure across European markets.

sector_stories.title: AI monitoring should be a standard part of investor due diligence
sector_stories.summary: Investors are increasingly prioritising continuous AI monitoring and audit trails during due diligence to mitigate risks of rogue AI behaviour and ensure compliance with upcoming regulations.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights growing enterprise and regulatory demand for robust, verifiable AI governance and production-level monitoring systems.

sector_stories.industry: UK stationery and Post Office retail
sector_stories.title: Fed questions whether falling shop theft figures tell the full story
sector_stories.summary: The Federation of Independent Retailers has questioned official ONS data showing a 2% decline in shop theft, citing retailer distrust in reporting processes and persistent crime levels.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights ongoing operational risks, security challenges, and the need for improved police engagement for independent retail chains.

sector_stories.industry: UK stationery and Post Office retail
sector_stories.title: ACS highlights increasingly violent shop theft in latest crime figures
sector_stories.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores reports that shop theft is becoming increasingly violent, with a 10% rise in recorded robberies as police refine their crime classification methods.
sector_stories.angle: Rising violence against retail staff necessitates enhanced security protocols and policy advocacy for the convenience sector.

sector_stories.industry: UK stationery and Post Office retail
sector_stories.title: Retail industry welcomes shoplifting decrease with caution
sector_stories.summary: Official ONS data shows a 2% decrease in shoplifting offences for the year ending June 2026, though retail industry bodies warn that violence against staff remains at epidemic levels.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights evolving retail crime trends, legislative delays in worker protections, and the ongoing operational focus on staff safety.

sector_stories.industry: UK stationery and Post Office retail
sector_stories.title: Consumer confidence takes a hit ahead of Budget
sector_stories.summary: BRC-Opinium data shows consumer confidence in the economy has dropped for the third consecutive month, while retail spending expectations have risen ahead of the festive period.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights macroeconomic headwinds and cost pressures impacting retail margins and consumer discretionary spending ahead of the Budget.

sector_stories.title: Is College Preparing Students for Work?
sector_stories.summary: Higher education institutions are increasingly integrating career readiness and professional development into the core undergraduate experience to better prepare students for an evolving, unpredictable labour market.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights a shift towards embedding employability and lifelong learning support directly into academic curricula and university services.

sector_stories.title: Could Tech Sovereignty Free Higher Ed From Big Tech?
sector_stories.summary: Higher education institutions are increasingly exploring digital sovereignty to reduce reliance on big tech vendors and gain greater control over their data, infrastructure, and AI strategies.
sector_stories.angle: Signals a shift in institutional procurement preferences towards open-source, vendor-agnostic, and cost-efficient AI infrastructure models.

sector_stories.title: Education Affordability a Priority for Voters
sector_stories.summary: A survey of 2,000 registered voters indicates that education affordability is a primary concern, with 66 percent favouring candidates who prioritise lower costs for education and training.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights strong bipartisan voter demand for affordable education pathways, potentially driving future federal policy and funding shifts.

sector_stories.title: Survey: 48% of Employers Say AI Will Make College Degrees More Important
sector_stories.summary: A Lumina Foundation and Gallup survey reveals that 48 percent of employers believe artificial intelligence will increase the importance of college degrees over the next five years.
sector_stories.angle: Validates the long-term market demand for higher education credentials despite rising public skepticism regarding degree value.

sector_stories.title: Fertility preservation in elite sports needs further consideration
sector_stories.summary: Elite sports federations are increasingly offering egg freezing to athletes, though experts highlight concerns regarding training compatibility, long-term funding, and potential pressure to delay motherhood.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights an emerging niche market for fertility preservation services and associated ethical and policy considerations for clinics.

sector_stories.title: Population studies are key to safe newborn genome screening
sector_stories.summary: Large-scale population studies are essential to address risks of overdiagnosis and incomplete penetrance when implementing whole genome sequencing for newborn screening programmes.
sector_stories.angle: Advances in genomic screening and variant interpretation directly impact the future of pre-implantation genetic testing and reproductive counselling.

sector_stories.title: Budget to be ‘most significant’ since Osborne era, says Glenigan
sector_stories.summary: Glenigan reports that construction activity is weakening, with project starts, contract awards, and planning approvals all falling significantly in the three months to September.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights market fragility and declining private residential demand, which directly impacts the pipeline for rooflight installations.

sector_stories.title: New towns at risk as building materials production slows, Lords warn
sector_stories.summary: A House of Lords committee warns that government uncertainty regarding new-town projects is discouraging investment and causing manufacturers to reduce building material production capacity.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights supply chain volatility and potential demand shifts for construction products linked to government infrastructure policy.

sector_stories.title: Fears devolution ‘complexity’ will ‘not put projects on site’
sector_stories.summary: Mace Consult warns that devolution policy complexity and declining new orders pose significant delivery risks to the UK construction sector despite potential long-term pipeline opportunities.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights market volatility, declining order volumes, and persistent material price inflation affecting the UK construction supply chain.

sector_stories.title: The Budget must build confidence and investment
sector_stories.summary: The UK construction sector faces rising insolvency rates, high fuel costs, and regulatory burdens, prompting calls for government stability and long-term investment incentives in the upcoming Budget.
sector_stories.angle: Highlights macroeconomic headwinds, supply chain fragility, and regulatory pressures impacting the broader UK construction and building products market.

sector_stories.industry: AI robotics for rail and aviation asset inspection
sector_stories.title: Google DeepMind uses Gemini 4 Argon to teach Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid new skills from video
sector_stories.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced a Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline using Gemini 4 Argon to autonomously teach humanoid robots physical tasks from video, significantly reducing manual simulation engineering time.
sector_stories.angle: Accelerates development cycles for autonomous inspection robots by automating complex simulation and physical skill acquisition.

sector_stories.industry: AI robotics for rail and aviation asset inspection
sector_stories.title: How AI Confidentiality Gaps Are Becoming a Liability for Robotics Firms
sector_stories.summary: Robotics firms face significant legal and security risks when employees input proprietary algorithms or confidential client data into public AI tools that train on user prompts.
sector_stories.angle: Critical infrastructure providers must enforce strict AI data governance to avoid NDA breaches and regulatory non-compliance.

sector_stories.industry: AI robotics for rail and aviation asset inspection
sector_stories.title: New ASTM standard aims to test how robots perform in the real world
sector_stories.summary: ASTM International is developing a new standard to measure how optical-signal degradation affects the task performance of mobile manipulators in real-world conditions.
sector_stories.angle: Standardised testing for sensor reliability under environmental stressors is critical for safety-critical rail and aviation inspection robotics.

sector_stories.industry: AI robotics for rail and aviation asset inspection
sector_stories.title: Neura Robotics launches multimodal AI model that gives robots perception and memory
sector_stories.summary: Neura Robotics has launched Neuron AI, a multimodal foundation model integrating 3D vision, touch, audio, and memory to enable robots to perform complex physical tasks.
sector_stories.angle: Advancements in multimodal physical AI and sensor fusion significantly improve autonomous inspection capabilities in complex, non-visual industrial environments.
